html:
Everything on a machine is, at the bottom, a bit: a sensor sees or does not, a valve is open or shut. These six instructions are the whole language of bits.

InstructionReadsDoes
XIC(tag)Examine If Closedpasses power when the bit is 1
XIO(tag)Examine If Openpasses power when the bit is 0
OTE(tag)Output Energizewrites 1 when the rung is true, 0 when it is false, every scan
OTL(tag)Output Latchwrites 1 when the rung is true; leaves it alone when false
OTU(tag)Output Unlatchwrites 0 when the rung is true; leaves it alone when false
ONS(storage)One Shotpasses power for exactly one scan after the rung ahead of it becomes true; the storage bit remembers the previous scan

OTE: the output that follows the rung

OTE is a mirror. The bit is whatever the rung is, scan after scan. Two rules follow. First, write each bit with OTE in one place only; the last OTE wins and the earlier one is wasted. Second, an OTE rung with a seal-in branch is how you make a bit remember (chapter 4).

OTL / OTU: memory without a seal-in

A latch sets the bit and walks away; nothing turns it off except an unlatch. Use the pair when the set and the reset belong to different events in different places, a request raised by one rung and cleared by another:

XIC(Cap_Req)XIC(LS7)OTL(Cap_Done);
XIC(Conv_Index)OTU(Cap_Done);

(Part IV, step 7: the capper’s ram reached the bottom, so this bottle has its cap; and when the belt steps, the next bottle is a new bottle.)

Latches survive a power cycle in a real controller and here survive everything short of Reset Sim, which is exactly why they need an unlatch you can find. Put the OTU right after the OTL in the listing when you can, and comment both.

ONS: once, not while

A push button held down is true for fifty scans. If the rung that counts presses were XIC(PB)ADD(Count,1,Count), one press would add fifty. ONS lets the rung through on the first scan only:

XIC(Enter)ONS(Enter_ONS)[CLR(Large_Bottle_Count),CLR(Small_Bottle_Count),CLR(Scrap_Bottle_Count),CLR(Scrap_Box_Count)];

(Part IV, step 9: one press of Enter clears the counts once, however long it is held.)

The storage bit (Enter_ONS) is a BOOL you create and never use anywhere else. OSR and OSF are the same idea as output instructions, with their own storage and output bits: OSR(storage,output) turns output on for one scan when the rung goes true, OSF when it goes false.

Try it

With the button-and-lamp project from chapter 4, add a DINT Presses and a BOOL PB_ONS. Write XIC(Start_PB_Pressed)ONS(PB_ONS)ADD(Presses,1,Presses); and watch Presses in Quick Watch (Alt+3) while you press. Then delete the ONS and press once.
